reports.title: Review Report of the Consolidated Condensed Interim Financial Statements

guidance.heading: Outlook for 2026
section: During the third quarter of 2026, traffic in the international segment maintained its positive trend and grew 2.8%, reaching a new all-time record for a third quarter, with 4.0 million passengers. In contrast, domestic traffic decreased 5.9%, mainly affected by Flybondi’s capacity reduction during July and the suspension of its operations in September. However, towards the end of the quarter, the other two main domestic airlines were able to absorb much of the unserved demand, allowing domestic traffic in September to recover to levels similar to those recorded in the same month of 2025. Overall, total passenger traffic reached 11.4 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 3.0%.

For the fourth quarter and the end of 2026, international traffic is expected to continue growing, albeit at more moderate rates due to increasingly demanding comparison bases. In the domestic segment, a gradual recovery is expected from the levels observed during the third quarter, although the year would close below 2025. Operations at Ezeiza will be partially constrained by the works on runway 17-35 and on the runway intersection planned for October and November, which will temporarily limit the operational length of the runway, with operating restrictions for certain larger aircraft.

Regarding commercial revenues, the third quarter showed a mixed performance. Cargo revenues continued to be affected by the reduction in average dwell times and by a demanding comparison base, despite growth in the volume handled, which was 11.0% above 2025. Duty Free revenues decreased due to a shift in the passenger mix towards low-cost airlines, with a lower average ticket, while VIP Lounge revenues were affected by lower conversion rates at Ezeiza and Aeroparque. These effects were partially offset by the start of internal operation of the passenger boarding bridges, opening a new revenue line, together with improvements in Food & Beverage, retail and aircraft services. For the end of the year, this dynamic is expected to continue, with a favorable evolution of the commercial segments.

Operating costs continued to be affected by the macroeconomic context, mainly by the evolution of wages and other services denominated in local currency, and by energy prices. In this scenario, the Company continues to implement cost control, efficiency and expense prioritization measures to moderate the impact on operating profitability, while monitoring the evolution of inflation and the exchange rate.

desk.headline: Filing is the Argentine unit AA2000's Q3 accounts, not group results: sales down 16% in real pesos, profit up on FX gains; concession extended to 2056
results: This filing holds the Q3 accounts of Aeropuertos Argentina 2000 (AA2000), CAAP's main Argentine unit, not CAAP's group results, which had not been published when this was written.
AA2000's sales fell 16% to ARS 369.1bn in inflation-adjusted pesos (annual inflation was 33%); aeronautical income fell 15% and commercial income 16%.
Operating profit dropped 36% to ARS 81.0bn, but net income nearly doubled to ARS 69.6bn on foreign-exchange gains on its dollar debt.
Passengers fell 3% to 11.4m: international traffic hit a Q3 record of 4.0m (+2.8%), while domestic fell 5.9% after Flybondi cut back and then suspended flights.
A new deal with the regulator, signed 1 Sep, extends the concession to 2056 (partly conditional on a US$600m investment plan); passenger fees are now set in US dollars.

guidance.summary: No numbers given. AA2000 expects international traffic to keep growing more slowly in Q4 and domestic traffic to recover gradually but end 2026 below 2025; runway works at Ezeiza limit some flights in Oct–Nov.

watch: CAAP's own Q3 group results and call, still to come.
Effect of the new dollar-based passenger fees from October.
Whether the US$600m funding condition for the full extension to 2056 is met by June 2027.
